claim_versions.claim: A blood pressure monitor comprising a blood pressure cuff (A) and a reference pressure sensor (B) positioned within an adjustable cavity design (C), wherein the adjustable cavity design (C) is configured to position the reference pressure sensor (B) at varying distances from the blood pressure cuff (A) in response to changes in cuff material or wear over time, and wherein the reference pressure sensor (B) is calibrated to detect changes in cuff material or wear over time.

redesign.new_claim: A blood pressure monitor comprising a blood pressure cuff (A) and a reference pressure sensor (B) positioned within an adjustable cavity design (C), wherein the adjustable cavity design (C) is configured to position the reference pressure sensor (B) at varying distances from the blood pressure cuff (A) in response to changes in cuff material or wear over time, and wherein the reference pressure sensor (B) is calibrated to detect changes in cuff material or wear over time.
redesign.change: Added a technical effect (detecting changes in cuff material or wear over time) and an operating condition (response to changes in cuff material or wear over time) to the claim.
redesign.reason: This revised claim should survive the prior-art attack because it adds a technical effect and an operating condition, which distinguishes it from the prior art. The prior art references (WO 2004/035201 and US 5,049,911) do not teach the specific technical effect of detecting changes in cuff material or wear over time, and the operating condition of responding to such changes. Therefore, a skilled person would not expect the combination of the two references to work as intended, and the revised claim should be considered novel and non-obvious.
